subject: general
question:
Match the common name of the bee with its scientific name.
 
 Column I (Common Name). Column II (Scientific Name) 
 1. Indian bee A. Apis mellifera 
 2. Rock bee B. Apis cerana indica 
 3. Little bee C. Apis dorsata 
 4. Italian bee D. Apis florae
solution:
The correct answer is __**4) 1-B, 2-C, 3-D, 4-A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indian Bee - Apis cerana indica:** The **Indian bee** is scientifically known as **Apis cerana indica**. It is a species of honeybee native to South and Southeast Asia, widely used in beekeeping practices in India. *Hence, 1-B is correct.*
 
• **Rock Bee - Apis dorsata:** The **rock bee**, or giant honeybee, is scientifically named **Apis dorsata**. It is known for building large, exposed colonies on cliffs or tall structures. *Hence, 2-C is correct.*
 
• **Little Bee - Apis florea:** The **little bee** is scientifically classified as **Apis florea**. It is a small honeybee species found in Asia, known for its simple nesting habits. *Hence, 3-D is correct.*
 
• **Italian Bee - Apis mellifera:** The **Italian bee**, a subspecies of the western honeybee, is scientifically named **Apis mellifera**. It is extensively used in commercial beekeeping due to its high honey production. *Hence, 4-A is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Apis cerana indica (Indian Bee):**
 
 
• Native to India and Southeast Asia, this species is resilient to local pests and diseases.
 
• It produces moderate quantities of honey and is often used in traditional beekeeping systems.
 
• It builds multiple combs in cavities and is adaptable to diverse climatic conditions.
 
 
 
• **Apis dorsata (Rock Bee):**
 
 
• This species is known for producing large quantities of honey.
 
• It builds nests in open spaces, such as rocks, cliffs, and tall structures.
 
• Due to its aggressive nature, it is not commonly used in domesticated beekeeping.
 
 
 
• **Apis florea (Little Bee):**
 
 
• A small bee species found in Asia, known for building single-comb nests on tree branches or shrubs.
 
• It produces small amounts of honey, which is often consumed locally.
 
• Its non-aggressive nature makes it less of a threat to humans.
 
 
 
• **Apis mellifera (Italian Bee):**
 
 
• A highly productive species commonly used in modern beekeeping practices worldwide.
 
• Known for its gentle behavior, large-scale honey production, and adaptability to artificial hives.
 
• This species is native to Europe and Africa but has been introduced to many other parts of the world.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Honeybee Species:** Honeybees are crucial pollinators for many crops and play a vital role in maintaining biodiversity.
 
• **Beekeeping Benefits:** Beekeeping contributes to honey production, wax production, and crop pollination, which enhances agricultural productivity.
 
• **Global Distribution:** Apis mellifera is the most widely distributed honeybee species, while Apis cerana, Apis dorsata, and Apis florea are mostly confined to Asia.
 
• **Conservation Efforts:** Protecting honeybee species is critical for sustainable agriculture and ecosystem health.
